'''Frederi G. Viens''' is an [[Americans|American]] [[statistician]] and [[mathematician]], and [[Academic staff|academic]]. He is a professor in the Department of Statistics at [[Rice University]], a founding member of the Diverse Rotations Improve Valuable Ecosystem Services Project,<ref name=khi>{{Cite web|url=https://www.drives-network.org/drivesteam|title=D.R.I.V.E.S. Team|website=D.R.I.V.E.S.}}</ref> a senior research contributor to the Sustainability of Agrarian Societies in the Lake Chad Basin initiative,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sustainabilitylakechad.com/people|title=The Lakechad Project|website=www.sustainabilitylakechad.com}}</ref> and moderator of the long-term scientific committee for the Seminar on Stochastic Processes conference series.<ref name=es>{{Cite web|url=https://depts.washington.edu/ssproc/index.php|title=Seminar on Stochastic Processes|website=depts.washington.edu}}</ref>

Viens' primary research areas are [[probability theory]], [[stochastic processes]], [[Quantitative analysis (finance)|quantitative finance]], and [[Bayesian statistics]]. His research collaboration has focused on different areas, including [[climate change]], [[Agroecology|agro-ecology]], [[agricultural economics]], [[development economics]], [[nuclear physics]], and human medicine. He was named a [[Franklin Fellows program|Franklin Fellow]] at the [[United States Department of State|US State Department]] in 2010<ref name=assi>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/news/2011/viens_franklin_fellow.html|title=Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs thanks Purdue for lending Frederi Viens to the State Department in 2010-2011. - Department of Statistics - Purdue University|website=www.stat.purdue.edu}}</ref> and Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2013.<ref name=ims>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imstat.org/wp-content/uploads/import/awardees_2013.pdf|title=IMS Fellows 2013}}</ref> He has an [[Erdős number]] of 3, via his co-authored paper with [[Paul Malliavin]] published in the ''[[Journal of Functional Analysis]]'' in 2010.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Airault|first1=H.|last2=Malliavin|first2=P.|last3=Viens|first3=F.|date=2010|title=Stokes formula on the Wiener space and n-dimensional Nourdin-Peccati analysis|journal=Journal of Functional Analysis|volume=258|issue=5|pages=1763–1783|doi=10.1016/j.jfa.2009.10.017}}</ref> His work has been published in journals, including ''[[Annals of Probability]]'', ''[[Annals of Statistics]]'' and ''[[American Journal of Agricultural Economics]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=U3OA6C4AAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|title=Frederi Viens|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

==Education==
Viens earned a Maîtrise in Pure Mathematics from the 
[[University of Paris VII|Université de Paris VII]] and a 
[[Master of Science|Master's degree]] in Mathematics from the 
[[University of California, Irvine]], both in 1991. He completed 
his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Mathematics from the University 
of California, Irvine in 1996, under the supervision of 
[[René Carmona]].<ref name=rice>{{Cite web|url=https://statistics.rice.edu/news/frederi-viens-joins-department-statistics-professor|title=Frederi Viens joins Department of Statistics as professor &#124; Department of Statistics &#124; Rice University}}</ref> Following his doctorate, he held an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] International Opportunities Postdoctoral Fellowship at the [[Universitat de Barcelona]] (1996–1997) and an NSF-[[NATO]] Postdoctoral Fellowship at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|Université de Paris VI]] (1998–1999).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stt.msu.edu/~viens/CV-Viens2022.pdf|title=Frederi Viens}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1997, Viens became an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University of North Texas]], holding this post until 2000. In 2000, he joined [[Purdue University]]'s Departments of Statistics and Mathematics as an assistant professor, was promoted to associate professor there in 2003 and professor in 2008. He served as Associate Director (2000–2003) and then Director (2003–2016) of the Computational Finance MS Program at Purdue, and as Associate Director of the Actuarial Science Undergraduate Program from 2007 to 2010. In 2016, he was appointed professor at [[Michigan State University]]'s Department of Statistics and Probability. In 2022, he joined Rice University, where he has been serving as full professor in its Department of Statistics, in the School of Engineering and Computing, and as Chair of the Department's Committee on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.<ref name=rice/>

Viens was a science adviser for the [[Bureau of African Affairs]] at the US State Department from 2010 until 2011.<ref name=assi/> Moreover, between 2015 and 2016, he served as program director in the Division of Mathematical Sciences at the [[National Science Foundation|US National Science Foundation]]. He also served as the chairperson of the Department of Statistics and Probability at Michigan State University between 2016 and 2020. At MSU, he also served as Adjunct Director of the Center for Statistical Training and Consulting (2018–2021) and Acting Director of the Data Science MS Program (2020–2022). He served as the director of the BS Program in Actuarial Science and Quantitative Risk Analytics from 2017 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stt.msu.edu/~viens/CV-Viens2022.pdf|title=Frederi Viens}}</ref>

==Research==
Viens' research spans several areas of mathematics, statistics, and their applications to the natural and social sciences.

'''Stochastic analysis'''

Viens has conducted research on stochastic processes, focusing on the existence and regularity properties of random processes in the context of [[stochastic differential equations]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tindel |first1=S. |last2=Tudor |first2=C.A. |last3=Viens |first3=F. |title=Stochastic evolution equations with fractional Brownian motion |journal=Probability Theory and Related Fields |date=October 2003 |volume=127 |issue=2 |pages=186–204 |doi=10.1007/s00440-003-0282-2}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref> He has also demonstrated the consistency of [[Estimator|statistical estimators]] in linear and nonlinear stochastic equations with long memory noise.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tudor |first1=Ciprian A. |last2=Viens |first2=Frederi G. |title=Statistical aspects of the fractional stochastic calculus |journal=The Annals of Statistics |date=July 2007 |volume=35 |issue=3 |doi=10.1214/009053606000001541 |arxiv=math/0609295}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref>

'''Quantitative finance and insurance'''

His research in quantitative finance has focused on improving the modeling of risk uncertainty in [[insurance]] and estimating [[stochastic volatility]] for [[Option (finance)|stock option pricing]], with findings offering insights for managing [[systemic risk]] in [[financial markets]] and improving [[risk management]] in financial sectors.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cofes.rice.edu/announcements/capturing-all-costs-quantifying-all-risks |title=Capturing all costs, quantifying all risks |publisher=Center for Computational Finance and Economic Systems, Rice University}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Irakoze |first1=Irène |last2=Nahayo |first2=Fulgence |last3=Ikpe |first3=Dennis |last4=Gyamerah |first4=Samuel Asante |last5=Viens |first5=Frederi |title=Mathematical Modeling and Stability Analysis of Systemic Risk in the Banking Ecosystem |journal=Journal of Applied Mathematics |date=16 November 2023 |volume=2023 |pages=1–10 |doi=10.1155/2023/5628621 |doi-access=free}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref>

'''Nuclear physics'''

Viens has evaluated the predictive power of [[mathematical models]] to improve the quantification of [[Nuclear binding energy|nuclear binding]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Neufcourt |first1=Léo |last2=Cao |first2=Yuchen |last3=Nazarewicz |first3=Witold |last4=Viens |first4=Frederi |title=Bayesian approach to model-based extrapolation of nuclear observables |journal=Physical Review C |date=24 September 2018 |volume=98 |issue=3 |article-number=034318 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.98.034318 |arxiv=1806.00552 |bibcode=2018PhRvC..98c4318N}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref> and the nuclear saturation point.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Drischler |first1=C. |last2=Giuliani |first2=P. G. |last3=Bezoui |first3=S. |last4=Piekarewicz |first4=J. |last5=Viens |first5=F. |title=Bayesian mixture model approach to quantifying the empirical nuclear saturation point |journal=Physical Review C |date=2024 |volume=110 |issue=4 |article-number=044320 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.110.044320}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref>

'''Agricultural economics and agroecology'''

His research in agricultural and developmental economics has advanced mathematical models for estimating economic risks, using [[Bayesian hierarchical modeling]] to analyze U.S. agricultural R&D's impact on productivity, assess uncertainties in R&D [[Distributed lag|lag structures]], and explore long-term policy implications.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baldos |first1=Uris Lantz C. |last2=Viens |first2=Frederi G. |last3=Hertel |first3=Thomas W. |last4=Fuglie |first4=Keith O. |title=R&D Spending, Knowledge Capital, and Agricultural Productivity Growth: A Bayesian Approach |journal=American Journal of Agricultural Economics |date=January 2019 |volume=101 |issue=1 |pages=291–310 |doi=10.1093/ajae/aay039}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref> His work in [[agroecology]] has examined how crop rotation diversity affects ecosystem resilience and agricultural productivity, contributing to the Diverse Rotations Improve Valuable Ecosystem Services (DRIVES) network.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.rice.edu/news/2023/rice-helping-study-how-soil-health-improvement-can-boost-crops |title=Rice helping study how soil health improvement can boost crops |publisher=Rice University News |date=2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ars.usda.gov/news-events/news/research-news/2024/diverse-crop-rotations-reduce-risk-of-crop-loss-under-poor-growing-conditions/ |title=Diverse Crop Rotations Reduce Risk of Crop Loss Under Poor Growing Conditions |publisher=USDA Agricultural Research Service |date=2024}}</ref>

'''Climate science'''

He has collaborated with climate scientists to help reconstruct Planet Earth's global mean [[surface temperature]]s over the past two millennia, including principled [[uncertainty quantification]] using Bayesian statistics.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Barboza |first1=Luis |last2=Li |first2=Bo |last3=Tingley |first3=Martin P. |last4=Viens |first4=Frederi G. |title=Reconstructing past temperatures from natural proxies and estimated climate forcings using short- and long-memory models |journal=The Annals of Applied Statistics |date=December 2014 |volume=8 |issue=4 |doi=10.1214/14-AOAS785 |arxiv=1403.3260}}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref> His research has also examined how climate variability influences the risk of armed conflict in specific regions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.rice.edu/news/2026/climate-patterns-may-shape-where-violent-conflict-risks-are-amplified-rice-study-finds |title=Climate patterns may shape where violent conflict risks are amplified, Rice study finds |publisher=Rice University News |date=2026}}</ref> He has conducted extensive fieldwork on the [[Lake Chad]] Basin in West-Central Africa, collecting and analyzing agricultural data to help local communities adapt to environmental and social uncertainties.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.rice.edu/news/2026/one-africas-most-studied-environmental-crises-rice-team-collecting-and-analyzing-missing |title=In one of Africa's most studied environmental crises, Rice team collecting and analyzing missing data |publisher=Rice University News |date=2026}}</ref>

'''Healthcare'''

His interdisciplinary research has also extended to healthcare, including studies on stakeholder incentive misalignment in the [[opioid crisis]] and the relationship between workplace bullying and patient safety outcomes in hospital settings.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boloori |first1=A. |last2=Arnetz |first2=B.B. |last3=Viens |first3=F. |last4=Maiti |first4=T. |last5=Arnetz |first5=J.E. |title=Misalignment of Stakeholder Incentives in the Opioid Crisis |journal=International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health |date=2020 |volume=17 |issue=20 |pages=7535 |doi=10.3390/ijerph17207535 |doi-access=free|pmc=7589670 }}{{primary source inline|date=March 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Viens is married to Carolyn Johnston, a history professor at Michigan 
State University. They have a daughter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.argus-press.com/news/news_local/article_a2cef5df-ac1b-55b0-8044-4faa8294e759.html|title=Lessons outside the classroom pay off|first=SALLY YORK Argus-Press Staff|last=Writer|date=April 7, 2019|website=The Argus-Press}}</ref> He and Johnston operate a small-scale sheep farm in [[Laingsburg, Michigan]], which also received a humane farming grant from the [[Food Animal Concerns Trust]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.farmworldonline.com/News/NewsArticle.asp?newsid=23953&fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAAR2EG-5Fy3W5wmN-zNIBKNyV0cQWu6Y5yDm-FZvnLyfafgBqVDU__7Y1fn4_aem_ye9KYPUZI8ojCu-h7nxa6g|title=Farm World – weekly farm newspaper source for ag news, classifieds, auctions|website=www.farmworldonline.com}}</ref> Viens has an [[Erdős number]] of 3, via his co-authored paper with [[Paul Malliavin]] published in the ''[[Journal of Functional Analysis]]'' in 2010.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Airault|first1=H.|last2=Malliavin|first2=P.|last3=Viens|first3=F.|date=2010|title=Stokes formula on the Wiener space and n-dimensional Nourdin-Peccati analysis|journal=Journal of Functional Analysis|volume=258|issue=5|pages=1763–1783|doi=10.1016/j.jfa.2009.10.017}}</ref>
